sense: of a picture or a scene

terms.gloss: background; the part of a picture that stands back
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.101: umbram aliquam et recessum (Lewis & Short: “somewhat of shade and background”)
terms.comment: Literally a going back, a retreat, and so a recess or the inner part of a place (Lewis & Short). Cicero takes it from painting for what stands back so that the lit parts stand out. Of a person in a photograph, Latin simply says what is behind him: post eum.

terms.gloss: the parts of a scene painted to look further away
terms.grammar: present participle of abscēdō used as a noun, neuter plural
evidence: Vitr. 7 praef. 11: alia abscēdentia, alia prōminentia esse videantur (M-O s.v. perspective)
terms.comment: Vitruvius on stage painting, beside prōminentia, the parts that seem to stand forward (the foreground). A participle, not a noun of its own.

phrases.latin: habeat illa in dīcendō admīrātiō ac summa laus umbram aliquam et recessum, quō magis id, quod erit illūminātum, exstāre atque ēminēre videātur
phrases.english: let admiration and the highest praise in speaking have some shade and background, so that what is lit may seem to stand out and come forward the more

sources: Lewis & Short: recessus · Lewis & Short: abscedo
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
